items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Function names are mostly clear (updateAftersalesPreview, renderStatsUI), but business loops use cryptic short names (`rf`, `rfi`, `p`, `v`, `l`). The non-obvious refund-proration logic in the preview has little explanation beyond one comment.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Everything is in one 2548-line file, which caps this at accept. Refund proration is duplicated in the UI (updateAftersalesPreview recomputes allFullyRefunded and rawSum*payable/subtotal). The item-collection loop is copy-pasted between updateAftersalesPreview and submitAftersalesUI.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Validation at the cart boundary fails: hidden tests test_cart_rejects_illegal_quantity, test_cart_rejects_out_of_stock_and_over_stock and test_coupon_threshold_and_invalidation all fail. The UI also uses `parseInt(qtyInput.value) \|\| 0` and silently drops bad quantities.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: submitAftersalesUI calls requestAfterSaleAPI directly with no confirm, and importDataUI overwrites data with no confirm. Only reset is shown with `confirm(...)`. A refund preview with its formula exists, but several dangerous actions skip confirmation.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The UI calls the same *API functions (requestAfterSaleAPI, getStatsAPI, importDataAPI), but money is float math with round2 (`round2(rawSum * order.payable / order.subtotal)`), and the UI preview duplicates the refund calculation.
